papers-please game sourced

Papers, Please

A border inspection game in which the player checks entrants' documents against daily-changing rules on a timed shift and spends the wages on a family's rent, food, and heat.

2013Lucas Pope (3909 LLC)Job simcluster c147 mechanics
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

core loop

read the day's rules -> inspect each entrant's papers -> interrogate, fingerprint, or scan discrepancies -> stamp approve, deny, or detain -> citations and bribes adjust pay -> pay rent, food, and heat -> next day adds rules

design notes

The inspection rules are predicates that accumulate day by day as the fictional state's politics shift, so the same entrant generator yields harder cases over time. Pay is per correctly processed entrant within a fixed shift and citations arrive by fax after each error, which makes speed and accuracy a direct trade. The household ledger converts that trade into moral pressure, and bribes and rule-bending choices feed scripted branches that lead to twenty endings.

relations

7 stored edges
uses

Treasury and budget

The end-of-day ledger adds wages and bribes, subtracts citation penalties, and requires paying rent, food, heat, and other necessities; going into debt ends the game.

core
uses

Daily action budget

Each shift is a fixed real-time working day and pay is per properly processed entrant, so processing speed trades against error risk.

core
uses

Rule-checking inspection

Each day adds or changes entry requirements; the player cross-checks passports, permits, and other papers, can interrogate, compare fingerprints, or order body scans, and receives faxed citations after protocol violations.

core
uses

Dilemma cards

Scripted entrants pose choices such as admitting a supposed spouse without complete papers, trading rule compliance against helping people.

supporting
uses

Needs decay

Family members' condition worsens on days when food, heat, or other necessities go unpaid.

supporting
uses

Procedural characters

Randomly generated entrants are mixed with scripted ones; the unlockable endless mode uses only generated entrants.

supporting
uses

Triggered event chains

EZIC contacts and other scripted encounters branch the story toward twenty endings, including escape to Obristan.
